claims.text: The initial material is an equiatomic or near-equiatomic FeCoNiTi high-entropy alloy.
The baseline FeCoNiTi alloy exhibits multiple ferromagnetic transitions.
The baseline FeCoNiTi alloy lacks a dominant sharp first-order magnetic transition.
FeCoNiTi contains distinct fcc and C14 Laves phases.
Adjusting the Fe, Co, Ni, and Ti ratios can promote a sharp first-order magnetic transition near room temperature.
Controlled phase separation or adjustment of the fcc-to-C14 phase balance is likely to produce the proposed first-order magnetic transition.
A first-order magnetic transition produces an abrupt change in magnetization.
An abrupt magnetization change at a first-order transition produces a substantial magnetic entropy change.
An abrupt magnetization change at a first-order transition produces a pronounced adiabatic temperature change.
The compositionally tailored FeCoNiTi alloy will have a larger magnetic entropy change than the baseline composition.
The compositionally tailored FeCoNiTi alloy will have a larger adiabatic temperature change than the baseline composition.
The predicted magnetocaloric enhancement will occur near room temperature under applied fields of approximately 1–3 T.
Fe, Co, Ni, and Ti provide a cost-effective and abundant elemental basis for the proposed magnetocaloric material.
Processing deviations may reduce the proposed magnetocaloric improvement.
Undesired secondary phases may reduce the proposed magnetocaloric improvement.

contradictions.description: The proposed mediator relies on controlled phase separation and tuning the fcc/C14 phase balance, whereas the experiment calls for thermal treatments to ensure phase homogeneity. A homogeneous state may suppress the two-phase structure proposed as the mediator.
